preserve-meaning.instruction: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code at every level.

scope-and-terms.instruction: Define scope, terminology, actors, and assumptions before normative behavior.

requirement-strength.instruction: Keep one clause per source rule, with its actor, condition, action and strength. Explain existing behavior in ordinary language when the supplied material does not use uppercase BCP 14 keywords and none are requested. When BCP 14 is used, declare the convention before the clauses, preserve the literal English keyword including qualified and negative forms in translation, and distinguish prohibition from technical inability. Facts, representations and calculations stay outside requirement clauses.

specification-structure.instruction: Use suitable abstract, introduction, technical sections, security considerations, and IANA applicability statements without inventing facts or registrations. For a word-limited internal excerpt, prioritize the requested actor, condition and behavior; include a section only if it contributes to that excerpt.

reference-role.instruction: A document supplying a requirement that an implementation must follow is normative for that behavior. Classify other material as informative only when it supplies background.
